_state_of_this_file: DEAD. This mechanism was designed on 2026-08-20 ~18:45, bootstrapped by chief round 108, and killed by measurement on 2026-08-20 ~20:35 without ever being taken by a single cloud round. It is kept, not deleted, because the reason it died is the most expensive lesson of that day and deleting it is how a project re-invents the same broken idea six months later. DO NOT WRITE TO THIS FILE. DO NOT READ IT AS A LOCK.
_why_it_died: The whole design rested on one true idea: a lock you win by WRITING a file is not a lock; a lock you win by PUSHING is, because git rejects a non-fast-forward push atomically and that rejection is real mutual exclusion.
The idea was correct and the implementation was impossible, for two independent reasons, both measured by cloud rounds 110 and 111 - the first two rounds that ever ran on the cloud:

1. This file lives on `main`, and a Claude Code Routine CANNOT PUSH `main`. The refusal happens at the sandbox layer, before GitHub is ever reached, and no prompt can override it. So the lock could never be taken - not contended, not lost: never taken, by anyone, once.

2. Moving it onto a branch does not rescue it either, because every Routine session is given a NEWLY RANDOMISED branch name (claude/eloquent-turing-pu97a8, then claude/keen-volta-pu97a8). There is no fixed ref for two rounds to race on, and a race is the entire mechanism.
A lock that cannot be contended is not a weak lock. It is not a lock.
_what_replaced_it: AN OPEN `claude/*` PULL REQUEST IS THE LOCK (Panya's ruling, 2026-08-20 ~20:35). At the start of every round the chief asks the GitHub API whether any open pull request has a `claude/*` head, in either repository. If one exists the round ENDS IMMEDIATELY. Both halves were measured before being relied on: round 111 read the GitHub API successfully, and rounds 110 and 111 each opened a pull request. Nothing in the replacement rests on anything untested - which is exactly what this file failed to do.
_who_releases_it: GitHub, never the chief. `.github/workflows/merge-claude-pr.yml` in each repository merges the pull request when the gate is green, and CLOSES it when the gate is red, when it will not merge cleanly, or when no verdict arrives at all (the scheduled `reap` job). A closed red pull request is not lost work: the branch is kept on purpose.
_correction_20260830: MEASURED FALSE, by pf_bridge#507 (ka1-A): a round can finish clean and push real work, then find BOTH the REST `draft:false` PATCH and the GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview` mutation rejected (403) for the agent's own token, leaving the pull request stuck as an open draft with no agent-side path to close it. 'Every path ends with the pull request not open' was true only as long as something always flipped draft to ready; it did not hold. The `reap` job now tries `gh pr ready` with the WORKFLOW's own token (which already has `pull-requests: write` and already merges/closes pull requests a few lines below) before treating a stale draft as dead; only a draft that refuses that too is closed. So the lock still cannot get stuck FOREVER - a stale draft is bounded by `PF_STALE_MINUTES` either way - but the bound is enforced by the workflow's token succeeding at ready-or-close, not by an agent token that has been observed to refuse both.
